newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU official concerned about "bit" tax plans.
newsitem.headline: EU official concerned about "bit" tax plans.

text.p: A senior official at the European Commission expressed concern on Wednesday over member states considering taxing the amount of information Internet users get out of the system.
Stefano Micossi, director general of DGIII (industry), said many member states were already considering "bit" (electronic unit transmitted) taxes.
"We are very concerned about it," he told a conference on the information society and electronic commerce. "The real issue is fear of erosion of national tax bases."
An EU advisory group has come up with the idea of taxing every "bit", but this suggestion has been greeted by a wave of protests from Internet users.

The advisory group, composed of academics, industry and labour representatives and others is expected to issue a final report shortly that will mention the "bit tax" in a broader discussion of the tax implications of global electronic commerce.
However, another EU advisory group, composed of media and telecommunications companies, has drafted a report urging the EU to reject the bit tax.
